Had a look at the formatting. Here's the current state string:

```
${model.name} [${format_token_to_string(inputTokens)}] \n\t- in[${format_token_to_string(chat.inputTokens)}] out[${format_token_to_string(chat.outputTokens)}] cached[${format_token_to_string(chat.cachedTokens)}]
```

Which renders like:
```
gpt-4o [12.34k]
	- in[45.67k] out[8.90k] cached[2.10k]
```

It's functional — shows per-request tokens on the first line and cumulative stats indented on the second. The tab and dash give it a tree-like look. But if you want it cleaner, you could:

1. Make it a single line: `gpt-4o [12.34k] | in:45.67k out:8.90k cached:2.10k`
2. Or add labels like `Model: gpt-4o | Tokens: 12.34k (in:45.67k out:8.90k cached:2.10k)`

What do you think? Cool as is or want a tweak?

Want me to clean it up? I can change it to a single-line format like:

```
${model.name} [${format_token_to_string(inputTokens)}] | in:${format_token_to_string(chat.inputTokens)} out:${format_token_to_string(chat.outputTokens)} cached:${format_token_to_string(chat.cachedTokens)}
```

That way it's more compact and readable at a glance. Your call.
